name: Ben-Hadad
bio: Ben-Hadad, son of Tabrimon and grandson of Hezion, was king of Aram, ruling from Damascus. When Baasha, king of Israel, fortified Ramah to blockade Judah, King Asa of Judah emptied the temple and palace treasuries and sent the silver and gold to Ben-Hadad, asking him to break his treaty with Baasha and attack Israel instead, recalling a treaty between their fathers. Ben-Hadad agreed, sending his army commanders to attack Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maacah, all Kinnereth, and the territory of Naphtali — a strike that forced Baasha to abandon Ramah and withdraw to Tirzah (1 Kings 15:18-21).
